To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there was no difference in the disability of patients with RA at 12 month follow up who had received multidisciplinary team care compared to usual care.
multidisciplinary team care has no significant impact on disability in people with rheumatological conditions.
multidisciplinary team care does not appear to be effective for the management of people with RA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effectiveness of MDT care for the management and treatment of RA.
the effectiveness of multidisicplinary team (MDT; also known as ‘interdisciplinary’) interventions for the management of rheumatoid arthritis.
the effectiveness of multidimensional interventions in the management of people with rheumatological conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is insufficient to support or refute the effect of MTD care on disability, activity or QoI in adults with RA.
there is no evidence that MDT care for people with RA is effective.
MDT care for adults with RA is likely to have no effect on disability at 2 or 12 months, disease activity at 12 month, or QoL at any time point.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evidence for the effectiveness of MDT care for people with RA was limited and that the evidence for effectiveness of MDT on disability, disease, activity and Qo.L is inconclusive.
MDT care does not appear to be effective in improving disability, disease activity, or QoL at the 12-month follow-up period.
MDT care is not effective for the management of RA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no evidence that multidisciplinary team care is effective for the treatment of RA.

there is limited evidence evaluating MDT care for people with RA and there is likely to be little or no effect of MTD care on disability at any time point or disease activity and quality at 12  months.
there is no evidence to support the use of multidisciplinary care teams in people with rheumatology conditions.
